Lessons.Title: Using Functions to Model Battery Power
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: analyze paired time/battery readings, build and critique a linear charging or draining model, make a justified prediction, and revise assumptions when new information appears. Independently authored Edulytiks adaptation from Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 4 Lesson 18, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/4/18/preparation.html and student tasks https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/4/18/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source culminates in battery power modeling rather than solely solving a linear formula.

First-party hypothetical charging data: after t minutes since connection, battery percentages are (0,5),(10,14),(30,32),(40,41), each consistent with increasing by9 percentage points per10 minutes. A simple line is B(t)=5+0.9t percent while charging is approximately linear. The physical battery percentage cannot exceed100 or fall below0; without further measurements a sensible model stops or changes at full charge.

Solving B(t)=100 gives 0.9t=95, so t=95/0.9≈105.56 minutes after plug-in (about1hour45.6minutes). This is an extrapolation beyond the observed40-minute data, not a precise claim about an actual phone. Real devices often change charge rate; the source asks learners to reflect critically and improve models.

Contrasting hypothetical drain case: an unplugged device begins at90% and loses approximately4 percentage points per hour, D(h)=90−4h on 0≤h≤22.5 until empty. At 5 hours D=70%; estimated time from90% to20% is17.5 hours. If battery state or rate changes, a piecewise function could be more suitable than one straight line.

Student activity: graph the first-party readings, justify fit/units, solve for predicted full-charge time, compare this to an alternative piecewise rate, and explain what extra observations are needed. Actual user-device measurements are optional and require explicit truthful collection and privacy handling. Teacher-scored rubric 0–2 for accurate data plot, valid model/rate, checked predictions, and critical uncertainty/model-revision explanation.

KeyConcepts.Title: Approximate linear model
KeyConcepts.Definition: A constant-change model approximates trends in paired data.

KeyConcepts.Title: Physical bound
KeyConcepts.Definition: Battery percentage must remain between0 and100 inclusive.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Restrict model range or replace rule when full/empty.

KeyConcepts.Title: Extrapolation uncertainty
KeyConcepts.Definition: Predictions outside observed input range depend on unverified assumptions.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Disclose observation range versus forecast range.
KeyConcepts.Example: 100% predicted at105.56min from data only through40min.

WorkedExamples.Title: Verify a charging trend
WorkedExamples.Question: Use (0,5),(10,14),(30,32),(40,41).
WorkedExamples.Method: Use an original function and check its rule, inverse, constraints, and units at multiple inputs.
Steps: From0 to10 the increase is9 in10min, slope0.9pp/min.
WorkedExamples.Check: All four hypothetical readings match this simple line.

WorkedExamples.Title: Predict full charge cautiously
WorkedExamples.Question: When does B(t)=100 under the model?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use an original function and check its rule, inverse, constraints, and units at multiple inputs.
Steps: Flag the extrapolation and possibility of slower charging near full battery.
WorkedExamples.Answer: About105.56min after plugging in, under unchanged-rate assumption.
WorkedExamples.Check: The output reaches physical upper bound at this input.

WorkedExamples.Title: Model a battery draining
WorkedExamples.Question: For D(h)=90−4h, find percentage after5h and time to20%.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use an original function and check its rule, inverse, constraints, and units at multiple inputs.
WorkedExamples.Check: Time is within the declared model domain.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Extending a straight charging line beyond100%
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Battery percentage cannot exceed physical capacity.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Cap or change the model and disclose assumption.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating extrapolated full-charge time as observed fact
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Only0–40min data were fabricated for model construction.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Confusing percent change with relative percent growth
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: A rise9 points from5% to14% is not 9% relative increase.

SummaryPoints: A function can summarize battery percentage versus time but needs physical bounds.
The invented charging data fit B(t)=5+0.9t over the measured segment.
Full-charge time105.56min is extrapolated and potentially unreliable.
Model choice, uncertainty and authentic device data require teacher review.
